name: Prize crossword No 26,741
preamble: Five across and seven down solutions involve, wholly or in part, some of 5 down and lack any further definition; 5 down itself is undefined.

clue.text: Force a writer to absorb Republican material

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it inside, so one piece ends up within another

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force
taken as written
a Bic is a familiar brand of ballpoint pen
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political story about pressuring a journalist to soak up Republican propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests a person, but here it is a pen: the Bic ballpoint takes in the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth, the woven stuff that clothes and curtains are made from.

clue.text: A cyclist

blocks.note: taken as written
Sir Chris Hoy is a Scottish track cyclist with six Olympic golds

explanation.walkthrough: As the preamble says, this themed answer has no definition. Hoy is also an island in Orkney, which makes it one of the British Isles hidden in the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahoy is the sailor's hail to another vessel; here the preamble stands in for any definition.

clue.text: Gulf citizens infringe rights

indicators.note: to infringe is to intrude or encroach, so one piece pushes inside another

blocks.note: people of Oman, on the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Gulf
RTS is an abbreviation of rights

explanation.surface: A complaint that people from the Gulf states are trampling on someone's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined, as the preamble says: the Isle of Man sits in the middle of ROMANISTS, a word for Roman Catholics.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanists is an old, often hostile term for adherents of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Start to chase game

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of chase
rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: A hunting instruction: begin pursuing the quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: the Hebridean island of Rum (Rùm) is inside. 'Game' looks like quarry in a chase, but it is a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or poor; the preamble replaces the definition here.

clue.text: Attempts to stifle objection

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother by wrapping round, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: attempts are tries
a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying to silence a dissenting voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: the Isle of Bute in the Firth of Clyde runs through the middle of TRIBUTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tributes are acts or gifts expressing respect; the preamble supplies the role of definition.

clue.text: (See special instructions)

blocks.note: surface reading: the clue simply sends you to the preamble
setter's reading: the preamble says this entry has no definition; the islands hidden in twelve other answers point to it

explanation.walkthrough: There is nothing to parse: crossing letters and the themed entries (Hoy, Rum, Bute, Sark, Coll, Unst, Iona, Man, Fair Isle and more) reveal the collective name.
explanation.definitionFit: The archipelago of Great Britain, Ireland and many smaller islands off north-west Europe is the theme every undefined entry draws on.

clue.text: Audacious place to sail off Cowes

blocks.note: a place is given by the preposition of location: you sail in somewhere
Cowes is on the Isle of Wight, facing the strait between the island and the mainland

explanation.surface: A daring sailing spot near a famous yachting town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes, on the Isle of Wight, hosts the Cowes Week regatta; the Solent is the strait between the island and mainland England.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacious can mean impudently bold, which is the sense of rude, cheeky disrespect.

clue.text: Consuming funny bar in the morning

indicators.note: bar here means except or excluding, so some letters are left out

blocks.note: funny means amusing
AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning

explanation.surface: Eating a comic chocolate bar for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a snack or a pub, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Using up a resource is consuming it, as fuel or time is consumed.

clue.text: Describing display is up to politician

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an expo is an exhibition or display
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Whether a showy presentation is for the politician to decide.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory Island, off Donegal, ends the entry, so it is themed too; the setter later said this definition crept in by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Expository writing explains or sets out facts, which is what describing does.

clue.text: Long sleeper put out, spanning old room

indicators.note: to span something is to stretch across it, so one piece reaches round another

blocks.note: to douse a fire is to put it out
O is a standard abbreviation for old
RM is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: Someone who sleeps a long time is turfed out of an old room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests annoyed or evicted; here it means extinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse hibernates for months, famously asleep at the Mad Hatter's tea party.

clue.text: Broadcaster hosts current politician, revealing lots

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
I is the physics symbol for electric current
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A TV channel has a topical politician on who spills plenty of secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing lots' sounds like disclosing secrets, but it describes skimpy clothes that show a lot of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy outfit covers little of the body, so it exposes plenty of flesh.

clue.text: He's fascinated by dates, or miso, cooked with gluten

definitions.note: a clause describing the person; the answer is the noun naming him

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foodie choosing between dates or miso cooked with gluten.
explanation.walkthrough: Dates look like the fruit in a kitchen scene, but they are calendar dates, the raw material of number mysticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A numerologist reads mystical significance into numbers, including those in birth dates.

clue.text: Arrest bishop taking drug

blocks.note: to collar someone is slang for arresting them
B is the chess notation for bishop
someone on a drug is taking it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A police raid nabs a clergyman with narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: Coll, an Inner Hebridean island, opens the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The collarbone is the clavicle, linking shoulder blade and breastbone; the preamble replaces a definition.

clue.text: Heartless deeds

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letters are cut out

blocks.note: deeds are doings

explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: the Isle of Dogs is a district in London's East End on a bend of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The entry stands only for the Isle of Dogs theme, with the preamble doing the defining.

clue.text: Resolve what cross may mean at a financial centre

blocks.note: a cross, X, is the Roman numeral for ten
taken as written
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Settling what an X means when it appears on a document at a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning determination. The City (of London) is the Square Mile of banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve and tenacity both name dogged determination to keep going.

clue.text: Thus was Caesar's Gaul in special novel

definitions.note: a statement describing the region; the answer is the adjective it implies

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A history lesson on how Julius Caesar's Gaul is portrayed in some special novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book in which Gaul appears; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans called northern Italy Gallia Cisalpina, Gaul on their own side of the Alps.

clue.text: Scot ordered to stop dirty stuff

indicators.note: things ordered are arranged afresh, so the letters are rearranged
a stopper plugs a gap from inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
gunk is informal for sticky dirt

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is told to stop being dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: Unst, the most northerly inhabited Shetland island, is hidden inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunstock is the wooden butt of a rifle held against the shoulder; the preamble defines it.

clue.text: Shots from short distances don't win in competitions

indicators.note: being inside something places one piece within another

blocks.note: not winning is losing
cup competitions, such as the FA Cup

explanation.surface: Players who shoot from close range never win any trophies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shots' suggests attempts at goal in a sports scene; it means camera shots.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a photograph or film frame taken with the camera near its subject.

clue.text: Small animal refuge

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the vessel Noah built to shelter pairs of animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A little sanctuary for animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is wholly an island name, so the preamble's theme serves as its definition.

clue.text: Popular board game finishes early

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
chess is played on a board

explanation.surface: A well-liked board game is over sooner than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: an inch is a Scottish and Irish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: Inches are small islands in Scottish and Irish place names; the preamble does the defining.

clue.text: Priest boxed here, for instead of against

indicators.note: one thing taking the place of another means a swap of letters

blocks.note: a priest sits enclosed in the box to hear confessions
pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A priest shut in a booth, arguing the case for rather than against.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: Iona, the Hebridean island of St Columba, sits near the end. 'Boxed' hints at a professional boxer but is not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional earns a living from a skill; the preamble takes the place of a definition.

clue.text: Nice money once smuggled into football club

indicators.note: going into something places one piece inside another

blocks.note: FC is the abbreviation for football club
to run goods is to smuggle them

explanation.surface: A tale of handy cash sneaked into a football club in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like pleasant, but it is the French city, so the money is French currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was France's currency, used in Nice until the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Loud song

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
an air is a tune or song

explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: Fair Isle lies between Orkney and Shetland, famous for its knitting patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair stands in the grid as part of the island name Fair Isle, which the preamble covers.

clue.text: African country rings airline to find island

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: Togo is a West African country
BA is British Airways

explanation.surface: A traveller in Africa phones an airline to track down an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like telephoning, but it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller Caribbean partner of Trinidad in the twin-island republic.

clue.text: Left a hotel and swindled a second one that's snooty

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to do someone is to cheat them, so did means swindled
taken as written
a second hotel, again H

explanation.surface: A guest checks out without paying and cons a second hotel, which turns out to be stuck-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to hotel, so 'a second one' is another H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lah-di-dah describes affectedly genteel, pretentious speech or manners.

clue.text: Mostly train a bird in film to make buns

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to train is to teach
taken as written
Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: Training a bird for a film role so it will bake buns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway but means teach.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light, fruited yeast bun, usually served toasted and buttered in Britain.

clue.text: Southern county

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
Kerry is a county in south-west Ireland

explanation.surface: A county in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Themed and undefined: a skerry is a small rocky islet, as in Sule Skerry off Orkney.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a reef or rocky islet, so the theme in the preamble covers it.
